name: Shell
summary: Shell is a global energy company working in oil and gas, chemicals, power and lower-carbon energy, and it hires graduates into technical, commercial and corporate roles. For its graduate programme, candidates commonly report online assessments and a recorded interview, followed by a final virtual assessment built around a case study shared in advance, a short presentation and questions from assessors. Experienced hires often go through recruiter screening and competency-based interviews.
rounds: Online assessments, often job simulations and questions about how you work
Final virtual assessment: a case study shared in advance, a short presentation and questions from assessors
looks_for: Analysing a situation and proposing practical solutions
Drive to achieve, and learning from feedback
Working well with people from different backgrounds
Honesty, integrity and respect for people
Understanding of the energy transition and commercial trade-offs

questions.text: Tell me about a time you analysed a messy situation and proposed a solution others adopted.
covers: The situation and why it was unclear
How you broke it down and what information you used
Your recommendation, how you won support and the result

questions.text: Tell me about an achievement you worked hard for. What drove you?
covers: The goal and why it was difficult
Setbacks and how you kept going
The result and what it says about you

questions.text: Tell me about a time you worked in a team of people from different backgrounds. How did you make it work?
covers: The team and the goal
A difference in views or styles and how you handled it
What the team achieved and your part in it

questions.text: Tell me about feedback that was hard to hear and what you changed because of it.
covers: The feedback and who gave it
Your honest first reaction
What you changed and the difference it made

questions.text: Tell me about a time you stopped or questioned something because it didn't look safe or right.
covers: What you noticed
How you raised it, even though it was uncomfortable
What happened next and what you learned

questions.text: How would you decide whether a company should invest in a new solar or wind project? Talk me through the factors.
covers: Demand, prices and long-term contracts for the power
Costs, risks, permits and grid connection
Comparing returns with other options, and the strategic fit

questions.text: Fuel sales at a group of service stations have dropped. How would you find out why?
covers: Checking the data: which stations, since when, which fuels
Possible causes: prices, competitors, roadworks, local events, service quality
Testing the most likely causes and proposing actions

questions.text: In two minutes, explain what the energy transition means for an energy company.
covers: The shift from fossil fuels towards lower-carbon energy over time
Effects on investment, products and customers
Balancing today's energy needs with lower emissions

questions.text: A pump at a plant keeps failing earlier than expected. How would you find the root cause?
covers: Safety first, then the failure history and operating data
Checking design limits, installation, operating conditions and maintenance
A root-cause analysis, the fix and monitoring afterwards

questions.text: You get a business case two days before a meeting. How would you prepare a five-minute recommendation?
covers: Reading for the key question and the numbers that matter
A clear structure: recommendation, reasons, risks, next steps
Preparing for tough questions and changes to the facts

questions.text: A project is behind schedule. How would you balance safety, cost and time to get it back on track?
covers: Safety is not traded away
Options: re-sequencing work, adding resources, cutting scope
Telling stakeholders honestly and agreeing the plan

questions.text: Why Shell, and why a career in energy?
covers: Something specific about Shell's businesses
Why energy matters to you, with a personal link
What you'd like to work on

questions.text: Which part of Shell's business interests you most, and why?
covers: One area, such as trading, retail, chemicals or lower-carbon energy
What you know about its challenges
How your skills fit

tips: In a case presentation, give your recommendation first, then the reasons, the risks and the next steps.
Expect follow-up scenarios after a presentation; candidates commonly report assessors changing the facts to see how you adapt.
Prepare stories that show how you analyse problems, what you've achieved and how you work with others.
Read about Shell's businesses and its plans for lower-carbon energy so you can discuss them in your own words.
Test your camera, microphone and connection before any virtual interview or assessment.
